tasks.short: Collect employee information through prescribed questions and confirm the answers.

steps.what: Check the prescribed questionnaire and instructions for this interview.
Look up existing employee details before asking for missing information.
Ask the employee the standard factual questions.
Clarify misunderstood questions and help the employee explain unusual circumstances.
Record the answers and read them back for employee confirmation.

loop.input: Structured answers and interviewer clarification notes.
loop.output: Draft answers mapped to questionnaire fields, with supporting note references.
loop.check: Validate field types; show every inferred mapping; require employee confirmation before submission.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt; unresolved fields return to the interviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured answers need no model, but free-text clarification notes need interpretation.

steps.what: Enter confirmed answers into the employee record.

tasks.design: Configure a questionnaire in the {HCM} or {WORKFLOW}, prefilled from authorised employee records, and remove questions without a justified collection purpose. Employees complete routine fields directly; interviewers handle clarification, while a bounded extraction loop prepares notes for employee confirmation and validated entry into the {HCM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interview scripts, notes and employee records sit apart. Unusual answers and accessibility needs make a single rigid form insufficient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form controls and record interfaces cover routine collection. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings and validation; bounded extraction can handle clarification notes.
tasks.still_hard: Accessible assisted completion, multilingual ambiguity and lawful collection of sensitive fields need careful design. Religion is special-category data under GDPR and is not a default HR intake field.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice confusion and help employees describe circumstances without steering their answers.

ambition.what: Accessible assisted intake for employees who cannot complete the standard digital form

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends more time on assisted intake and ambiguous answers. They gain discretion to choose the assistance channel, while substantive HR decisions remain with authorised roles.

reach.learn: Field ownership, effective dates and the difference between recording facts and approving changes.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee self-service changes flowing to payroll; this supports the records pattern, not this complete intake design.
Forms, prefilling and validation can replace routine interviewer collection; the time shares and build estimates are planning assumptions.
GDPR requires a justified purpose and an appropriate legal basis, including additional conditions for special-category data.

assumptions: The HR interpretation is factual employee intake, not candidate assessment.
Time shares describe an illustrative interview with clarification, not measured company data.
The interviewer remains available for assisted completion; employee effort does not disappear.
Automatic writes cover confirmed factual fields, not pay, benefit or employment decisions.
Build ranges assume one questionnaire and one employee-record interface. Consultation and access ranges cover working effort; external waiting may be longer.
Conversation-heavy priors fit clarification, but routine factual collection is sufficiently structured for configured forms.
unknowns: Which questions are actually asked and why each field is required.
Available self-service features, record interfaces and write permissions.
The proportion of employees needing assisted completion.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which accessibility and language options reduce assisted-completion failures?
Can existing field controls support the questionnaire without custom code?
new_work: Review unmatched note-to-field mappings.
Maintain questionnaire versions and collection purposes.
Handle failed submissions and duplicate records.
Check assisted-completion accessibility with employees.
tasks.statement: Ask questions in accordance with instructions to obtain various specified information, such as person's name, address, age, religious preference, or state of residency.

tasks.short: Clarify inconsistent interview answers and record agreed corrections.

steps.what: Read interview forms and identify answers needing clarification.

loop.input: Completed interview form, question definitions and fixed consistency rules.
loop.output: Possible contradictions with exact answer references and neutral clarification prompts.
loop.check: Validate field references mechanically; interviewer checks meaning before using prompts.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair attempt per form; unresolved items return to interviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch missing fields and impossible dates; contradictions in narrative answers require language interpretation.

steps.what: Compare disputed factual details with authorised employee records.
Ask neutral follow-up questions and explain unclear wording.
Decide whether answers are resolved or require specialist escalation.
Update the interview form and retain the correction history.

tasks.design: A rules check on the {WORKFLOW} validates interview forms and compares authorised fields from the {HCM}. A bounded model loop drafts narrative inconsistencies and neutral questions for interviewer review. The interviewer conducts clarification, decides corrections and approves the update to the {HCM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative answers lack fixed rules, while checking records and writing corrections require separate screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation and approval features cover structured checks. AI-assisted coding makes the comparison and bounded drafting components cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguity, distress and conflicting accounts need careful questioning. GDPR purpose limits, access controls and national rules constrain reuse of employee information.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, recognise misunderstood questions and distinguish uncertainty from an actual contradiction without judging credibility automatically.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one recurring questionnaire ambiguity for a wording trial.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less record comparison and correction entry, with more time for difficult conversations. Within delegated questionnaire standards, the interviewer can propose and run a small wording trial; employment decisions remain with authorised HR roles.

reach.learn: Question design, purpose limitation and how to test wording without changing required information.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee self-service changes flowing into HR and payroll records; this supports the record-update component.
Rules can compare structured fields; narrative contradiction prompts require local evaluation and human review.
The step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The HR setting involves employee intake and questionnaire clarification, rather than eligibility or loan decisions.
Interview forms have stable question identifiers and authorised employee-record links.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and include access review and any employee consultation required under national rules.
The model receives only information needed for clarification and produces no credibility or employment suitability scores.
unknowns: Which interview types, languages and sensitive fields occur?
Does the {HCM} support form amendments with correction history and approval?
Who may approve questionnaire wording trials?
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: How accurately can rules and a bounded model distinguish genuine contradictions from different interpretations?
Which existing {HCM} validation and amendment features can replace custom code?
new_work: Review suggested contradictions and reject unsupported interpretations.
Maintain question definitions and consistency rules.
Handle failed record matches and access exceptions.
Sample correction histories for accuracy and inappropriate data reuse.
tasks.statement: Identify and resolve inconsistencies in interviewees' responses by means of appropriate questioning or explanation.

tasks.short: Compile interview answers, apply questionnaire codes and file the results.

steps.what: Assemble reviewed answers and the current questionnaire codebook.
Transcribe answers from notes or completed forms into the result template.

loop.input: Reviewed answer forms and the result template.
loop.output: Structured answers with a source passage for each extracted field.
loop.check: Copy structured fields directly; validate types and completeness. Interviewer reviews narrative extraction and unreadable fields.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per form; unresolved fields remain blank for manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Direct mapping handles digital fields, but variable notes and free-text forms require bounded extraction.

steps.what: Assign questionnaire codes to answers and resolve ambiguous classifications.

loop.input: Accepted structured answers and a versioned questionnaire codebook.
loop.output: Suggested codes with supporting passages and an unresolved category.
loop.check: Use exact mappings first. Reject codes outside the codebook; interviewer approves narrative classifications.
loop.stop: One classification pass per answer; ambiguous or unsupported mappings go to the interviewer without repeated guessing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed choices map deterministically; open answers can express the same category in many ways.

steps.what: Enter accepted coded answers into the employee record.
File source forms and link them to the result record.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to collect answers once, apply exact code mappings and link source forms in the {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and classification loops handle legacy forms and narrative answers, with interviewer approval before a deterministic connector writes accepted results to the {HCM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms and codebooks differ across teams. Moving answers into records is repetitive, while narrative coding needs interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms remove much transcription. AI-assisted coding reduces connector effort, and constrained models can propose codes from a supplied codebook.
tasks.still_hard: Poor source notes, changing category definitions and inconsistent human coding limit quality. Historical records may need separate migration work.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve the respondent's meaning and challenge categories that erase important distinctions.

ambition.what: Provide a monthly anonymised report on recurring employee questionnaire themes.

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends less time copying and filing, and more time resolving difficult coding cases. They can recommend codebook revisions; decisions about employee outcomes remain with authorised HR roles.

reach.task: Identify recurring learning needs from employee questionnaires.
reach.learn: Theme analysis, aggregation thresholds and the difference between a reported need and a training recommendation.

evidence.claim: AFAS demonstrates self-service HR record changes; it does not establish automatic narrative questionnaire coding.
Rossum demonstrates document extraction, validation and exception routing in order processing, an adjacent pattern.
The proposed extraction and coding review times require a local pilot.

assumptions: Codes describe questionnaire answers, not applicant suitability, employee performance or eligibility.
Reviewed answers come from the preceding quality-review task; factual clarification is not repeated here.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates for mixed digital forms and narrative notes.
Build ranges assume reuse of shared form and review components; task ranges are not additive.
Access and applicable consultation under national rules are included; local procedures can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Current codebook, coding disagreements and ownership of category definitions.
Proportion of structured answers versus narrative or handwritten forms.
Whether the {HCM} accepts imports with source links and duplicate protection.
Permitted purposes, retention periods and reporting group sizes.
research_questions: How closely do proposed codes match independently reviewed human coding?
Which codes can be assigned through exact mappings alone?
new_work: Review extracted answers and ambiguous codes.
Maintain codebook versions and exact mappings.
Monitor failed writes and duplicate records.
Check that aggregate reports do not expose individuals.
tasks.statement: Compile, record, and code results or data from interview or survey, using computer or specified form.

tasks.short: Review interview answers for missing information, recording errors and inconsistencies.

steps.what: Retrieve interview answers and the applicable questionnaire instructions.
Check required fields, dates, allowed values and questionnaire branching.
Compare narrative answers with interview notes and flag possible recording errors.

loop.input: Interview answers, available interview notes and validation findings.
loop.output: Possible contradictions or omissions, each linked to its source passage.
loop.check: Require source references; interviewer accepts or rejects each proposed clarification. Never infer missing answers.
loop.stop: One comparison pass and one repair pass per questionnaire; unsupported findings go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch field errors but cannot reliably compare differently phrased narrative answers.

steps.what: Ask the respondent to resolve missing answers and meaningful contradictions.
Save confirmed corrections and mark the questionnaire reviewed.

tasks.design: Configure validation and a review queue in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to questionnaires in the {DOCS} and records in the {HCM}. A bounded comparison loop proposes source-linked questions; the interviewer resolves ambiguity with the respondent and approves corrections before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questionnaire versions, interview notes and records are separate. Narrative consistency checks resist simple field rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form validation handles routine checks. AI-assisted coding makes connectors and comparison tools cheaper to build; bounded text comparison helps with narrative exceptions.
tasks.still_hard: Notes may be incomplete. Consistent answers can still be factually wrong, and sensitive contradictions require a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparent error reflects uncertainty, misunderstanding or a sensitive disclosure.

ambition.what: Choose questionnaire wording changes from a weekly review of recurring clarification reasons.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking every field to resolving exceptions and improving question wording. The interviewer can propose wording changes; approval rights remain with the questionnaire owner.

reach.learn: Question design, field definitions and how downstream records use each answer.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee self-service changes flowing into HR and payroll records.
Source-linked narrative comparison is a proposed design; the digest contains no direct interview-review case.

assumptions: The baseline is employee questionnaire review in a mid-size European HR team.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
A review checks recording quality and completeness; it does not prove the respondent's statements.
Access review and employee consultation under national rules, where applicable, are included in the access range.
unknowns: Questionnaire formats, volumes and version controls.
Whether interview notes are retained and accessible.
Available interfaces and permissions in the {HCM} and {DOCS}.
Applicable national consultation requirements and local review responsibilities.
research_questions: How reliably can narrative contradictions be detected without inventing missing information?
Which existing form controls can express branching and cross-field validation?
new_work: Review proposed narrative discrepancies.
Maintain questionnaire versions and validation rules.
Sample accepted records for missed errors.
Maintain permissions, retention settings and connector failures.
tasks.statement: Review data obtained from interview for completeness and accuracy.

tasks.short: Contact employees, secure participation, and arrange survey interviews.

steps.what: Check the contact list, approved invitation, and previous contact attempts.
Send individual survey invitations using the approved wording.
Telephone employees, address participation concerns, and establish willingness to be interviewed.
Agree an interview time and send the booking details.
Record participation responses, bookings, and failed contact attempts.
Send reminders to eligible employees who have not replied.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW} to send approved invitations through the {EMAIL}, offer available slots from the {CALENDAR}, and maintain a contact log. Declines stop reminders automatically, while employees with participation concerns or access needs are routed to the interviewer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invitations, calendar bookings, and contact outcomes lived separately. Staff filled the gaps manually because the survey volume did not justify a custom application.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and workflow features can cover routine contact administration. Small adapters and exception views are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, reluctance, shift patterns, and inaccessible contact channels remain personal problems. Routine sends require approved wording, permitted recipients, and clear stopping rules.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer can hear hesitation, explain participation choices, and accept a refusal without turning the exchange into persuasion.
tasks.altitude: Routine invitations and scheduling take less time, leaving room for difficult contacts and shift-friendly appointments. Within an approved schedule, the interviewer can offer alternative times and channels; survey scope stays with the human resources specialist.

reach.task: Plan employee survey outreach across shifts and worksites.
reach.learn: Participation barriers, accessible channels, working-time constraints, and voluntary participation.

evidence.claim: Approved templates, booking links, reminder limits, and stop-on-decline rules can use existing workflow configuration.
AFAS demonstrates employee self-service and connected HR workflows, but the digest does not document survey outreach automation.
The proposed time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The main setting is employee survey outreach, usually by work contact details rather than household visits.
Routine invitations and reminders already have approved templates and recipient rules.
Human call outcomes are captured once through a short form; no call recording or speech analysis is needed.
The low whole-task automation prior remains relevant because participation conversations stay human. Electronic administration is more prominent here than in field enumeration.
unknowns: The actual split between invitations, telephone contact, and field visits.
Which channels employees can access during their working patterns.
Permitted reminder frequency and how refusals are recorded.
Available scheduling features and delegated appointment authority.
Applicable national rules for employee consultation and working time.
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration support interviewer availability and alternative formats?
Which invitation details improve comprehension without pressuring participation?
new_work: Handle bounced messages, failed bookings, and access requests.
Record human call outcomes through the short form.
Maintain templates, reminder limits, and available interview slots.
Check that declines and completed interviews suppress further contact.
tasks.statement: Contact individuals to be interviewed at home, place of business, or field location, by telephone, mail, or in person.

tasks.short: Help people understand and complete HR applications or questionnaires.

steps.what: Select the correct form and check which supporting information is needed.
Explain unfamiliar questions and the form's completion instructions.

loop.input: The respondent's question, selected form and approved completion instructions.
loop.output: A plain-language explanation with references to the applicable instructions.
loop.check: Show approved field help first. Interviewer reviews novel explanations; unsupported questions are escalated.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt per question; missing guidance triggers human help.
loop.why_not_simpler: Configured help covers standard questions; unfamiliar phrasing and contextual questions need bounded language interpretation.

steps.what: Help the respondent express answers and obtain missing supporting information.
Check required fields and attachments before reading the form back.
Read back the completed answers and obtain the respondent's confirmation.
Send the confirmed form to the responsible HR team.

tasks.design: Configure accessible forms in the {WORKFLOW}, with branching, attachment checks and approved help from the {DOCS}. A bounded answer desk drafts explanations for the interviewer, while the respondent confirms answers before routing to the {HCM}; assisted completion remains available.
tasks.previous_blocker: Static forms expose every question at once, and guidance is separate. Staff repeatedly explain the same fields and forward completed documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured branching, validation and routing already handle routine completion. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting them, while bounded drafting helps explain unfamiliar wording.
tasks.still_hard: Language barriers, disability, low literacy and sensitive disclosures require adaptable human help. A form cannot supply evidence or decide what the respondent means.
tasks.human_edge: Help someone give their own answer without steering it, and recognise when they need a different form of support.

ambition.what: Offer assisted remote completion appointments for shift workers unable to attend daytime HR desks.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer routine explanations and submission checks, with more scheduled support for difficult cases. The interviewer gains capacity to organise assisted sessions; eligibility and employment decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Accessible form design, assisted digital support and internal routing requirements.

evidence.claim: AFAS demonstrates employee self-service changes feeding HR and payroll processes.
TOPdesk Robin demonstrates knowledge-based answering with handover through a pre-filled request.
Accessible branching forms and respondent confirmation can reduce completion support; the estimated savings are unvalidated.

assumptions: The baseline covers internal employee applications and questionnaires, not loan or public-benefit eligibility.
The mailbox is used for final routing, not assumed to dominate the whole task.
Live completeness checks here precede the separate detailed review of interview accuracy.
Respondent confirmation authorises submission; it is not treated as GDPR consent or an employment decision.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The access range includes consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Actual form types, languages and accessibility needs.
Existing self-service, branching and help capabilities.
Who may assist, confirm and submit each form.
Which attachments are necessary and how long they must be retained.
Demand and staffing availability for remote assisted appointments.
research_questions: Which approved field explanations resolve most questions without model drafting?
Can users with different accessibility needs complete and confirm the configured forms?
new_work: Maintain form versions, branching and approved explanations.
Review novel drafted explanations.
Provide assisted sessions and resolve missing evidence.
Monitor abandoned forms, failed submissions and accessibility problems.
tasks.statement: Assist individuals in filling out applications or questionnaires.

tasks.short: Verify coverage for employee services and arrange payment where coverage is incomplete.

steps.what: Collect the service request, provider details and authority to request coverage information.
Check the provider portal for current coverage and authorisation requirements.
Read coverage conditions, exclusions and any unresolved provider qualifications.

loop.input: Provider response, applicable coverage wording and requested service.
loop.output: Coverage conditions, limits, expiry dates and unresolved questions with source passages.
loop.check: Validate amounts and dates against the source; benefits specialist confirms the summary.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; ambiguous coverage returns to the provider through a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Provider qualifications may be narrative. Structured responses bypass the model entirely.

steps.what: Calculate the uncovered amount using service prices and confirmed coverage.
Discuss the uncovered amount and permitted payment options with the employee.
Approve the arrangement and issue the confirmed payment terms.

tasks.design: An access-controlled case in the {WORKFLOW} requests minimum coverage data through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and stores the response in the {DOCS}. A bounded loop extracts narrative terms, deterministic calculations in the {ERP} show the uncovered amount, and approved payment terms are issued only after employee acceptance and finance approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coverage terms differ between providers, access is fragmented and negotiated arrangements need accountable approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Where provider interfaces exist, ordinary integrations can retrieve coverage. Bounded extraction can prepare a checked summary of narrative terms, while calculations remain plain code.
tasks.still_hard: A coverage check is not a payment guarantee. Provider access, disputed coverage, sensitive information and regulated financing arrangements may dominate cost.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty clearly and discuss affordability without pressuring the employee into an unsuitable arrangement.

ambition.what: A pre-service estimate of uncovered employee costs

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends less time navigating provider records and calculating amounts. They can present approved options earlier; they gain no authority to grant coverage, credit or payroll deductions.

reach.task: Resolve unclear benefit coverage with providers.
reach.learn: Coverage terminology, provider evidence requirements and boundaries between estimates and binding commitments.

evidence.claim: Provider integration, checked extraction and deterministic cost calculations are a proposed architecture; the digest contains no direct benefits-verification case.
GDPR imposes additional conditions on processing health data; an employee's operational authorisation alone does not establish every required legal basis.
Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects are constrained by GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: This is a conditional benefits-service intake scenario. Insurance verification and service financing are not typical duties in every HR department.
The employer has a legitimate role in coordinating payment; clinical records and diagnoses remain outside interviewer access.
A supported provider interface exists. Without one, portal checking remains manual and the integration estimate must be revised.
Payment options come from an approved policy. Credit underwriting and payroll deductions require separate assessment and authority.
Employee acceptance is recorded before finance issues binding terms.
Time shares describe this specialised scenario. The API-heavy prior is not proof that a particular provider offers access.
Build ranges cover one provider. Consultation, contracting and access waiting can be substantially longer than working effort.
unknowns: Whether this task exists in the customer's HR remit.
Which providers permit coverage queries and through which interfaces.
Who is liable for uncovered charges and whether financing involves regulated credit.
Applicable GDPR bases, special-category conditions and national rules.
Who can approve arrangements and how employee acceptance is recorded.
research_questions: What does each provider response establish, and how long is it valid?
Which proposed payment options require specialist credit or employment-law review?
new_work: Review extracted coverage qualifications.
Handle unavailable providers and stale coverage responses.
Maintain provider mappings, prices and payment policies.
Reconcile estimates against final charges and provider payments.
tasks.statement: Ensure payment for services by verifying benefits with the person's insurance provider or working out financing options.

tasks.short: Find invalid or missing interview data, investigate the cause and report unresolved problems.

steps.what: Check completed intake records against required fields and validation instructions.
Compare exceptions with interview notes to understand missing or inconsistent answers.

loop.input: Validity exceptions and relevant clarification notes.
loop.output: Suggested problem category with quoted supporting passages and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Require source passages and an allowed category; interviewer confirms interpretation.
loop.stop: One classification pass; unsupported or ambiguous cases remain unclassified for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect missing fields, but narrative contradictions and misunderstood questions require reading.

steps.what: Contact the employee to clarify the problem and request corrections.
Write an unresolved-data report and send it to the responsible HR specialist.

loop.input: Reviewed exception assessment, correction notes and report template.
loop.output: Draft report separating observed facts, attempted corrections and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Every factual claim links to a record or note; interviewer reviews before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; incomplete evidence produces a template for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative causes vary; fixed fields alone do not explain why collection failed.

steps.what: Decide whether to accept, correct or escalate the disputed data.
Record the resolution and update the exception status.

tasks.design: Run explicit validation rules on intake records in the {HCM} and manage exceptions in the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded loops classify narrative problems and draft evidence-linked reports; interviewers clarify answers and HR specialists approve disputed resolutions before the {HCM} is updated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Validation instructions were separate from collection screens. Explanations and resolutions were scattered across notes and the {EMAIL}.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable checks handle objective defects. Small reading and drafting loops can prepare the narrative work without deciding whether an employee is credible.
tasks.still_hard: An unusual answer may be valid. Resolving conflicting accounts, changing a poorly designed question and deciding whether collection is appropriate still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a confusing question from an unreliable answer and investigate without treating employees as suspects.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on recurring questionnaire defects

tasks.altitude: The interviewer handles fewer mechanical checks and brings documented patterns to a weekly intake review. They can propose question changes; the HR process owner approves them.

reach.learn: Root-cause analysis, evidence standards and correction versus escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Deterministic checks can detect missing fields and incompatible values; narrative review and estimated savings remain design assumptions.
The documented Amsterdam welfare case shows that automated flags did not establish better judgement than caseworkers; it is a caution, not an HR result.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: This task checks information quality rather than fraud, employee performance or hiring suitability.
Objective validation is separated from accepting disputed facts.
Shares include the HR specialist handoff and are illustrative.
The low-rule-coverage prior fits interpreting exceptions, while completeness checks have higher rule coverage.
Build ranges cover an initial rule set and one intake workflow; access and consultation waiting may exceed the stated working effort.
unknowns: Existing validation rules and exception volumes.
Who may accept disputed data or authorise corrections.
Whether notes are sufficiently complete to support classification.
National rules governing consultation if exception data could monitor staff.
research_questions: Which validation rules produce false alarms on legitimate employee circumstances?
Can recurring defects be reported in aggregate without exposing individual interview notes?
new_work: Review narrative classifications and draft reports.
Investigate false alarms and missed defects.
Maintain validation rules when questionnaires change.
Monitor unresolved cases and their assigned owners.
tasks.statement: Identify and report problems in obtaining valid data.

tasks.short: Explain survey aims and procedures, clarify questions neutrally, and check understanding.

steps.what: Read approved survey objectives, question guidance, and privacy information.
Explain the objectives, procedure, participation choices, and privacy terms.
Listen to the employee's query and identify what they have misunderstood.
Consult question guidance and select a neutral clarification.

loop.input: Question identifier, approved wording, approved clarifications, and a minimal interviewer-written description of the query.
loop.output: A short clarification draft with the approved source passage.
loop.check: Validate question and source identifiers. The interviewer checks meaning, neutrality, and unchanged response options before speaking.
loop.stop: Use exact approved guidance first. For an uncovered query, allow one draft and one repair, at most 800 output tokens; otherwise show original wording and refer the issue to the survey owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Lookup handles standard queries. An unfamiliar phrasing may need a constrained paraphrase; a new definitive interpretation remains with the survey owner.

steps.what: Check the clarification, explain it, and confirm the employee's understanding.
Log the question and clarification used for the survey owner.

tasks.design: Configure an explanation pack and searchable approved guidance from the {DOCS} in the {WORKFLOW}. For uncovered queries, a bounded drafting loop proposes a sourced clarification that the interviewer checks before speaking; the {WORKFLOW} logs the confirmed guidance identifier without storing the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance existed, but searching it during a conversation interrupted the exchange. Unusual misunderstandings still required careful human paraphrasing.
tasks.enabler_now: Search and template assembly already solve routine preparation. A small model loop can draft unfamiliar paraphrases, with source checks and human approval at delivery.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent paraphrase can alter a question or lead the answer. Understanding, accessibility, confidentiality concerns, and genuinely ambiguous survey wording remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer notices uncertainty, changes pace, and checks understanding without suggesting which answer the employee should give.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less guidance searching and note preparation, leaving room for scheduled clarification sessions. The interviewer can choose approved explanations, but gains no right to change survey meaning or privacy commitments.

reach.task: Create accessible facilitator guidance for employee questionnaires.
reach.learn: Plain language, neutral questioning, comprehension checks, and alternative presentation formats.

reach.task: Review whether survey participation creates avoidable access barriers.
reach.learn: Accessible participation routes and when an individual accommodation needs specialist review.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base and hands unresolved questions into a pre-filled request; this supports retrieval and escalation.
Neutral survey paraphrasing needs validation against question intent; the digest contains no documented case proving this particular loop.
EU AI Act classification depends on intended use; narrow procedural support and recruitment assessment require different treatment.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: This is employee survey explanation, not candidate ranking or an employment decision.
A maintained interview guide defines question intent and approved clarifications.
The assistant is visible only to the interviewer and does not address employees directly.
No recording, emotion inference, or employee scoring is introduced.
The priors correctly identify a conversation-heavy task with little drudgery. Most conversation time remains; preparation and paperwork can still change.
Automatic logging stores only the guidance identifier the interviewer confirms as used.
unknowns: Whether approved clarifications exist and who may authorise new ones.
The frequency and complexity of comprehension queries.
Languages, accessibility needs, and permitted processing of employee queries.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access approvals.
Whether the survey's intended use would change its EU AI Act classification.
research_questions: How many queries can exact approved guidance answer without a model?
Which paraphrase tests detect altered meaning or leading language?
What minimal query description supports drafting without including personal survey answers?
new_work: Check each proposed clarification before delivering it.
Refer ambiguous question meanings to the survey owner.
Maintain approved guidance and its version history.
Sample confirmed clarifications for neutrality and meaning preservation.
Maintain prompt limits, source checks, and fallback behaviour.
tasks.statement: Explain survey objectives and procedures to interviewees and interpret survey questions to help interviewees' comprehension.

tasks.short: Answer patient service calls, explain administrative information and route medical or financial questions.

steps.what: Answer the call, establish the request and verify identity when needed.
Find authorised administrative details in the patient administration system and guidance.
Explain routine administrative information and clarify what help the patient needs.
Select the appropriate clinician or billing specialist and make a warm handover.
Record the contact outcome and agreed follow-up in the patient administration system.

tasks.design: Connect the {TELEPHONY} to an authorised administrative view of the patient administration system in {OTHER}, with approved guidance from the {DOCS}. Configure referral choices and contact templates in the {WORKFLOW}; the interviewer keeps the conversation, specialist handover and approval of the contact record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patient details, guidance and referral contacts sit in separate places. Staff must search while supporting someone who may be distressed.
tasks.enabler_now: Read-only connectors, indexed guidance and configured contact templates are established technology. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort without requiring automated medical interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Identity checks, health-data access and specialist availability remain demanding. A service interviewer cannot resolve clinical questions or negotiate financial exceptions without the relevant authority.
tasks.human_edge: Notice distress, explain patiently and ensure that a vulnerable person reaches an accountable specialist.

ambition.what: Provide scheduled assisted callbacks for patients who cannot complete digital administration.

tasks.altitude: Less call time goes into searching and repetitive records, leaving more capacity for difficult conversations and assisted callbacks. Clinical and financial decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Create service training for sensitive patient conversations.
reach.learn: Accessible communication, referral protocols and the boundary between administration and clinical advice.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk Robin retrieves knowledge-base answers and creates pre-filled requests, an adjacent service-desk pattern.
Administrative retrieval and contact templates can support a human conversation without a model loop.
Health information requires special-category data safeguards under GDPR.

assumptions: This occupational task applies to a patient-facing employer or service unit; it is not typical internal HR work.
Where no patient service exists, this task is outside the local role.
The interviewer provides administrative assistance and routes clinical or financial decisions to authorised specialists.
The design uses no call recording, emotion analysis or model access to clinical records.
Time estimates preserve substantial human conversation, consistent with the task's high relationship and harm sensitivity.
The access range includes health-data permissions and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether the employer has a patient-facing service unit.
Patient administration interfaces and permitted administrative fields.
Identity verification, urgent escalation and referral procedures.
Availability of clinicians, billing specialists and accessible callback arrangements.
Applicable national consultation and health-sector requirements.

Which routine questions already have approved, accessible guidance?
new_work: Maintain approved guidance and referral contacts.
Review and complete templated contact records.

Manage callback queues and audit health-data access.
tasks.statement: Perform patient services, such as answering the telephone or assisting patients with financial or medical questions.

tasks.short: Prepare evidence-based reports answering specific questions about interview findings or collection problems.

steps.what: Clarify the report question, intended audience and required decision.
Retrieve relevant interview forms and authorised employee-record extracts.
Reconcile records and calculate relevant counts, categories and missing responses.
Interpret findings, investigate gaps and decide which conclusions the evidence supports.
Write the report with supporting tables, limitations and proposed next steps.

loop.input: Approved findings, calculated tables, report brief and report template.
loop.output: Draft report with evidence references and explicit limitations.
loop.check: Check all numbers against tables; reviewer verifies claims and references against findings.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per report; unsupported sections remain blank for the interviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates generate tables and standard text; explaining case-specific findings requires language drafting.

steps.what: Approve the report and share it with authorised recipients.

tasks.design: A scoped job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieves authorised records from the {HCM} and {DOCS}, reconciles them and generates checked tables. A bounded drafting loop turns human-selected findings into a report in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} releases the report to approved recipients after review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is dispersed, record definitions differ and each report asks a slightly different question. Collecting records and drafting prose therefore remain intertwined.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable queries and document templates handle collection and calculation. AI-assisted coding reduces their implementation cost, and bounded drafting handles the narrative after findings are selected.
tasks.still_hard: Small samples, missing answers and ambiguous causes limit conclusions. GDPR purpose limits and re-identification risks constrain employee-level reporting.
tasks.human_edge: Frame a useful question, recognise evidence gaps and refuse conclusions the data cannot support.

ambition.what: Monthly questionnaire-friction report identifying questions that repeatedly require clarification.

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends less time collecting records and formatting reports, and more time investigating why forms fail. They gain room to recommend a specific collection-process change; authority to alter HR policy does not change.

reach.learn: Basic data quality analysis, sampling limits and separating association from cause.

evidence.claim: Structured retrieval, reconciliation, calculation and templated reporting can use deterministic code.
A bounded model can draft from approved findings; human interpretation and publication review remain necessary.
The digest contains no documented case establishing automation rates for this HR reporting task.

assumptions: Reports concern interview findings and collection quality rather than automated employment recommendations.
Structured answers and stable record identifiers support deterministic tables.
Free-text evidence remains available for human interpretation rather than being silently converted into facts.
Build estimates cover one report family, authorised extracts and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Which report questions recur and which require fresh investigation?
Are interview forms structured, scanned or mixed?
Which recipients may see individual responses?
What aggregation and small-group disclosure rules has the organisation approved?
research_questions: Which report sections can existing {HCM} exports and templates generate?
How often do source records disagree, and which source should govern each field?
What review method reliably detects unsupported narrative claims?
new_work: Maintain field mappings, calculations and report templates.
Resolve missing records and reconciliation failures.
Review narrative claims and recipient permissions.
Monitor disclosure risks as report audiences and datasets change.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports to provide answers in response to specific problems.

tasks.short: Locate survey participants and list authorised contact addresses.

steps.what: Check survey coverage and which contact fields are necessary.
Find employees, worksites, and permitted contact details in employee records.
Compare contact details with previous forms and flag missing or conflicting addresses.
Telephone employees to resolve missing addresses or unclear contact preferences.
Merge confirmed details, remove duplicates, and save the survey contact list.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted participant view in the {HCM}, then use a small integration to compare permitted contact fields with structured forms in the {DOCS}. A records app in the {WORKFLOW} holds unresolved discrepancies and produces the survey contact list after employees confirm corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different record formats, restricted access, and unclear ownership made small integrations expensive relative to manual list building.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and configurable views handle most work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort needed for field mapping, validation, and a small exception screen.
tasks.still_hard: An address match does not establish permission to contact someone. Conflicting records, private addresses, and any household sampling require a clear purpose and human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer recognises when an address request is intrusive and can explain its purpose without pressuring the employee.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less searching and list maintenance, with more time for unresolved contact cases. No additional decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Resolve discrepancies in employee contact records.
reach.learn: Record ownership, effective dates, correction procedures, and field-level access.

evidence.claim: Filtering rosters, checking required fields, and deduplicating stable identifiers need deterministic rules.
AFAS supports HR self-service record changes and downstream payroll flows; this supports the record-update pattern, not household enumeration.
The proposed time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: Routine HR survey coverage concerns employees and worksites. Household enumeration is unusual and is not assumed.
Private postal addresses are used only when the survey needs postal contact.
Previous contact forms contain identifiable fields that can be compared without interpreting free text.
The priors support substantial gathering work and human resolution of missing data. The HR setting gives more weight to employee records than field visits.
unknowns: Whether household sampling is actually part of the remit.
The permitted survey purpose, contact fields, and reuse of existing records.
Available exports, stable employee identifiers, and record quality.
Applicable national rules for employee consultation and the local approval route.
research_questions: Can a configured participant view replace a separate contact list?
Which address checks reliably flag discrepancies without silently changing valid addresses?
new_work: Resolve flagged discrepancies and route permanent corrections to the record owner.
Maintain field mappings and duplicate rules.
Remove expired contact lists and review access permissions.
Check that changes in survey scope do not expand data collection unnecessarily.
tasks.statement: Locate and list addresses and households.

tasks.short: Submit completed interview assignments and discuss progress and blockers with the supervisor.

steps.what: Gather completed forms and check that assignment evidence is present.
Write a separate summary of completed and outstanding assignments.
Send completed assignments and the progress note to the supervisor.
Review submitted work and confirm acceptance or required corrections.
Discuss progress, resolve blockers and agree next priorities.

tasks.design: Configure an assignment queue in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to completed forms in the {DOCS} and relevant status fields in the {HCM}. Completion checks create a live progress view and notify the supervisor, replacing the separate progress note. Supervisors approve completed work in the queue, and conversations focus on blockers and priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion evidence and assignment status sit apart, so daily meetings compensate for weak shared visibility.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow configuration can provide queues, approvals and notifications. A small deterministic integration connects form completion to assignment status.
tasks.still_hard: A complete form can still contain poor information. Workload conflicts and sensitive exceptions require discussion, and staff-status visibility needs proportionate access under GDPR and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Raise concerns early, negotiate priorities and recognise when apparent delay reflects a difficult interview rather than poor progress.

ambition.what: Same-day reassignment of blocked interview cases.

tasks.altitude: Routine submission and progress recaps shrink, leaving shorter conversations about exceptions. Within an agreed queue policy, the interviewer can flag reassignment needs immediately; the supervisor retains acceptance and allocation authority.

reach.learn: Queue triage, handoff criteria and recording blockers without exposing sensitive interview content.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents HR self-service workflows, supporting the feasibility of connecting employee records and process status.
Assignment queues, completion checks and notifications can use deterministic workflow configuration without a model.
Reduced meeting time and build ranges are estimates; they depend on how much discussion is routine status reporting.

assumptions: The daily meeting combines work acceptance, routine status reporting and exception discussion.
Completion can be detected from agreed form and assignment states.
The future submission uses links and status metadata rather than emailing additional copies of confidential forms.
Access and consultation estimates cover any review required under national rules for employee-status visibility.
unknowns: Is supervisor acceptance required for every assignment or only selected cases?
Where are assignments currently recorded?
What proportion of the meeting concerns routine status versus substantive support?
Which status fields may supervisors and other interviewers see?
research_questions: Can an existing {WORKFLOW} queue link directly to the authoritative form record?
Which completion checks reliably identify missing paperwork without implying substantive acceptance?
new_work: Maintain assignment states and completion checks.
Handle broken form links and failed notifications.
Review acceptance exceptions and overdue blockers.
Keep queue access and notification recipients current.
tasks.statement: Meet with supervisor daily to submit completed assignments and discuss progress.

tasks.short: Collect employee survey responses, reconcile records, and report participation and findings.

steps.what: Gather previous survey records and the employee roster for the reporting period.
Ask survey questions and note answers during scheduled telephone interviews.
Transcribe interview notes into the survey workbook.
Check duplicates, missing responses, period boundaries, and participation totals.
Assess coverage gaps and distinguish useful patterns from misleading comparisons.
Prepare the survey summary and obtain approval before sharing it.

tasks.design: Use structured forms in the {WORKFLOW} for direct responses and interviewer-assisted entry, removing later transcription into the {SPREADSHEET}. A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles authorised records, applies agreed aggregation and small-group suppression rules, feeds the {BI}, and fills a report template in the {DOCS} for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper notes, archived records, and changing survey definitions made repeatable reporting difficult. Separate collection and reporting tools required manual transcription.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable forms can capture answers once. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build repeatable imports, validation checks, and report templates without a model interpreting every response.
tasks.still_hard: Non-response bias, ambiguous questions, historical coding differences, and small groups can undermine conclusions. Free-text theme analysis would need a separate design and validation exercise.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer understands how answers were elicited and can challenge a tidy result that conceals poor coverage or leading questions.

ambition.what: Weekly allocation of follow-up interviews to underrepresented worksites

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from transcription and tallying toward coverage checks and assisted interviews. If scheduling authority is delegated, the interviewer can allocate follow-up appointments weekly; the human resources manager retains policy and employment decisions.

reach.task: Assess whether employee survey findings support an HR intervention.
reach.learn: Sampling, non-response bias, aggregate confidentiality, and the limits of causal claims.

evidence.claim: Structured capture, duplicate checks, reconciled counts, and template reports can use deterministic software.
AFAS demonstrates HR self-service and record flows; this is adjacent evidence for direct capture, not a documented survey reporting case.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; this design produces aggregate reporting, not employee decisions.
The remaining assisted-interview time and build ranges are estimates requiring local measurement.

assumptions: This task concerns employee surveys and HR operational records. Public population enumeration and patient records are outside the assumed remit.
Most answer fields are structured; free-text answers are retained without automated theme coding.
Objectives and question explanations are handled in the separate explanation task.
Some employees can answer directly, while assisted interviews remain available.

No individual employment recommendations are generated.

Survey definitions, historical formats, and reliable denominator records.
Whether responses are identifiable, pseudonymous, or anonymous.
Approved reporting audiences, retention periods, and minimum reporting group sizes.
Delegated authority over follow-up scheduling.
Applicable national consultation requirements.

How should coverage be measured when response identities cannot be linked to employee records?
Which aggregate views reveal participation gaps while preserving confidentiality?

Maintain survey versions, reporting definitions, and denominator rules.
Review coverage bias and small-group disclosure before publication.
Support employees who need assisted completion.
Check report templates after survey or source-field changes.
tasks.statement: Collect and analyze data, such as studying old records, tallying the number of outpatients entering each day or week, or participating in federal, state, or local population surveys as a Census Enumerator.

tasks.short: Supervise interview staff and coach them in accurate, respectful information collection.

steps.what: Review completed interview forms and select examples for coaching.
Choose coaching priorities and staff support needs.
Prepare guidance, demonstrations and practice interview scenarios.

loop.input: Approved guidance, selected learning objectives and fictional practice facts.
loop.output: Draft demonstrations, practice scenarios and answers linked to guidance.
loop.check: Lead interviewer checks answers, tone, source references and absence of real employee details.
loop.stop: One pack and one revision per session; unsupported examples use approved templates.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard lessons; varied natural-language scenarios need bounded drafting.

steps.what: Demonstrate interviewing, observe practice and give individual feedback.
Assign follow-up practice and agree a review date.
Record training completion and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: A small dashboard in the {BI} brings together sampled form defects and training completion from the {LMS}. A bounded drafting loop creates practice material from approved guidance in the {DOCS}, while the lead interviewer selects priorities and coaches staff. Configured {LMS} workflows issue approved assignments and record attendance and follow-up dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coaching depends on observation and relationships. Preparing relevant examples and reconciling training records adds work across separate tools.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured learning workflows handle routine administration, while a bounded drafting loop reduces scenario preparation. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of assembling a small quality dashboard.
tasks.still_hard: Fairly interpreting mistakes and giving difficult feedback remain human work. Employee-level quality data requires GDPR controls and assessment of consultation duties under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confidence, workload and misunderstanding; adapt coaching and give feedback that staff can use.

ambition.what: Fortnightly refresher clinic for occasional interviewers.

tasks.altitude: The lead interviewer spends less time assembling materials and entering attendance. They can offer refresher clinics and assign practice within an agreed training programme; formal personnel decisions retain their existing approval route.

reach.task: Design and evaluate short interviewer refresher sessions.
reach.learn: Learning objectives, practice design and checking whether skills transfer to real interviews.

evidence.claim: Training assignment, attendance and completion can use configured learning workflows.
Bounded drafting can prepare practice material, but this digest provides no case validating automated interviewer supervision.
Time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates for a small pilot.

assumptions: An experienced interviewer supervises a small group as part of the role.
The pilot supports coaching without generating employee rankings or automated performance decisions.
Attendance confirms participation; it does not automatically certify interviewing competence.
Access and consultation estimates include any employee monitoring review required under national rules.
unknowns: How many staff need supervision, and how often do they interview?
Which {LMS} assignment and attendance features are already licensed?
May interview forms be reused for coaching, and under what access restrictions?
Who authorises training changes and signs off competence?
research_questions: Which recurring form defects are useful coaching signals without becoming misleading staff scores?
Can existing {LMS} configuration cover follow-up practice without a separate application?
new_work: Check generated scenarios and maintain approved training material.
Review dashboard signals in context.
Correct attendance and assignment exceptions.
Evaluate whether refresher clinics improve form accuracy and interview conduct.
tasks.statement: Supervise or train other staff members.

tasks.short: Handle HR office enquiries, maintain staff records and coordinate applicable service billing and receipts.

steps.what: Read incoming enquiries and identify the responsible team.

loop.input: Enquiry text and an approved routing taxonomy.
loop.output: Queue assignment and a minimal case description.
loop.check: Use explicit routing rules first; validate allowed queues and access restrictions.
loop.stop: One classification pass; ambiguous or sensitive cases enter a restricted manual triage queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text enquiries may lack explicit routing terms. Structured submissions use rules only.

steps.what: Find the applicable HR guidance and answer the enquiry.

loop.input: Enquiry and current, authorised HR guidance passages.
loop.output: Draft response with supporting guidance references.
loop.check: Check source version and employee access; HR assistant approves before sending.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one draft; missing or conflicting guidance triggers specialist referral.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied wording and context need a short tailored explanation; fixed requests use templates.

steps.what: Enter authorised staff changes into the employee record.
Forward approved service charges and payment terms to finance.
Prepare and issue the invoice against the authorised billing instruction.
Match incoming payments to invoices and record outstanding balances.

tasks.design: Use the {HELPDESK} for enquiry routing and reviewed answers grounded in current {DOCS}, while configured approvals feed authorised changes into the {HCM}. Where service billing belongs to this desk, the {WORKFLOW} passes approved charges to the {ERP}, which generates reviewed invoices and matches exact payment references from the {BANK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: A shared mailbox connects enquiries, employee changes and finance handoffs. Each team re-enters information because authorisation and record identifiers do not travel with the request.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured case routing, employee self-service and invoice matching already cover much of the work. Bounded loops are useful only for unstructured routing and response drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive enquiries need restricted queues. Record-change authority, disputed charges and unmatched receipts still require clear ownership and human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a routine enquiry masks a grievance, hardship or confidential issue and arrange the right human response.

ambition.what: A single status view for employee requests and related service charges

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time forwarding messages and copying approved changes. They can coordinate stalled cases across HR and finance, without gaining authority to approve benefits or waive debts.

reach.task: Check employee-change effective dates before the payroll cutoff.
reach.learn: Payroll cutoffs, correction procedures and which changes require separate payroll approval.

reach.task: Separate routine policy enquiries from cases needing confidential handling.
reach.learn: Escalation criteria, restricted access and neutral case summaries.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee self-service changes flowing to payroll and HR questions grounded in collective-agreement material.
TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base or opens a prefilled request, supporting the answer-and-handover pattern.
Approved invoice generation and exact-reference payment matching can use configured finance controls; these estimates are not documented case results.

assumptions: This broad occupational task is interpreted primarily as HR enquiries and staff-record administration.
Telemarketing and patient billing are sector-specific variants, not assumed general HR duties.
The billing steps apply only to the specialised employee-service scenario described in the coverage task.
Time shares illustrate a desk with that billing remit and include finance handoffs. A general HR desk needs a different allocation.
Approved staff changes already contain the required authorisation; automation does not approve substantive employment changes.
Payment matching accepts exact, unambiguous matches; partial, duplicate and disputed payments become exceptions.
The mailbox share is higher than the supplied prior because this scenario uses a shared mailbox for cross-team handoffs.
Build ranges assume existing systems and supported interfaces. National consultation and access waiting may exceed working effort.
unknowns: Which office duties actually belong to this role.
Whether the desk handles any billable employee services.
Existing enquiry queues, guidance ownership and response volumes.
Supported interfaces and approval controls across HR and finance.
National rules and consultation requirements if new reporting could monitor employees.
research_questions: Can current enquiry and self-service configuration remove the mailbox handoffs?
Which payment exceptions need manual investigation rather than automatic allocation?
new_work: Review answer drafts and maintain current guidance.
Handle restricted, ambiguous and misrouted enquiries.
Investigate failed employee-record updates.
Review invoices and reconcile unmatched payments.
Maintain routing rules, permissions and integration alerts.
